idiom_name: explicit projection (field whitelist or field mask) applied at one seam, before the receiver sees the message
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: decide the retained field set per receiver, express it as data (a mask or whitelist) or as a type (a narrow view), then apply it at exactly one seam - a channel adapter, the consumer's edge, or an API/output boundary. The projection keeps the retained fields, drops the rest and may flatten nested repeating groups into a flat element list, and it must always keep the message identifier and correlation fields. Where the message schema is available, validate the projection against the producer's schema so an upstream rename fails loudly instead of producing a quietly partial message; where it is not, pin the projection with a contract test over a recorded producer message. Keep an unfiltered copy out of band whenever audit, replay or reconciliation may need the dropped fields. Placement: producer-side filtering re-couples the producer to every receiver's needs - prefer receiver-side or channel-adapter placement where the producer is shared infrastructure.
code_sketch:
project(msg, KEEP):
    out = {}
    for k in KEEP:                      # KEEP = the receiver's field whitelist
        if k in msg: out[k] = msg[k]
    assert 'id' in out                  # correlation fields survive every projection
    return out

# placement: producer side couples the producer to every receiver; receiver side
# couples each receiver to the producer's schema - choose it deliberately.
pitfalls: Forwarding the whole message 'for now': the wide payload becomes the de facto contract and narrowing it later breaks consumers.
Removing the identifier or correlation fields along with the payload fields, so retries, deduplication and tracing stop working.
Destroying the only copy of the removed fields and discovering later that audit or reconciliation needs them.
Treating the projection as authorization: the hidden field is usually still reachable by another route.
Stringly-typed field names: a typo in a field mask produces a silent partial message instead of an error - prefer typed projections (DTOs, view classes) where the compiler catches renames.
Schema evolution drift: a producer adds or renames a field and the filter silently drops it from all receivers that have not updated their projections.

Wrong move: filtering by exclusion (remove known-secret fields) instead of by whitelist -> a producer adds a new sensitive field and it ships to every receiver on its first day -> instead enumerate the fields the receiver is allowed to have, so new producer fields are absent until deliberately admitted.

Wrong move: rely on the projection to keep hidden data away from an untrusted reader -> post-filtering leaves side-channels (timing, counts, scores) that rich queries can amplify into full reconstruction of the supposedly hidden records -> instead enforce authorization before the data is produced or retrieved and treat the projection only as a disclosure-reduction layer.

Wrong move: apply the same projection by excluding fields inside each receiver's business logic -> the receiver's contract is invisible, the exclusion logic duplicates across handlers and silently diverges -> instead materialize the projection as one named artifact (view class, DTO, SMT or mask) at the seam and let handlers consume only that type.
